name: scroll-snap-card-track
display_name: A swipeable track of text cards, with no JavaScript behind it
description: Cards laid out in a horizontally scrolling track that snaps to each card. Swiping, trackpad scrolling and tabbing through the cards' own links all move it; nothing is scripted.

contract.outcome: the track scrolls horizontally and settles aligned to a card edge (scroll-snap x mandatory) — the visitor is never left between two cards
contract.actor: visitor gesture (swipe / trackpad / shift-scroll) or the browser's own focus scrolling
contract.evidence: shipped page CSS: overflow-x auto + scroll-snap-type x mandatory + scroll-snap-align start; verified present in the live HTML

contract.outcome: a real page load of that card's destination, with a visible focus ring when reached by keyboard
contract.evidence: live page: 2 cards carry links (one external site, one mailto); the rest carry none

states.condition: the card record has no link URL
states.outcome: no anchor is rendered at all — the card is a piece of text, not a control that goes nowhere
states.why: `no-inert-control`, FOURTH independent sighting and the first at TEMPLATE level (`{{if .link_url}}`): three different authors, three different mechanisms, one rule. That is the case for naming it once in the register rather than rediscovering it per component.
states.evidence: template conditional; live page renders links on 2 of its cards only

states.outcome: the "Swipe or scroll →" hint is decorative and is hidden from assistive technology (aria-hidden), because it describes a pointer gesture that is not how a screen-reader user moves through the track

degraded_states.outcome: unchanged — there is none to fail

checks.note: a horizontally scrolling track must NOT make the PAGE scroll horizontally — the two are different, and this check distinguishes them by container
